Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 8cfeb470da8b70280a1b61e4d8b295b937077611
Please see the comments on [pdr: Add pldm_pdr_delete_by_sensor_id() API](https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/78461)
Acknowledged

I think this missed the point a bit. There should be no skipping of data involved, all the data should actually be extracted. But I think for clarity's sake we need to be explicit about whether the extracted data is protocol vs host endian, and to indicate that we should have structures that aren't packed for host-endian data.

Let me take some time to poke at this myself.
This still needs to be resolved.
Andrew, I have tried to extract the whole structure as discussed, I hope this is the right way, and I will make further changes based on your suggestion.
You're not using the value of `pdr->hdr.type` before calling `pldm_msgbuf_complete()` below, so there's no need to test the return value here.
Acknowledged
This is still skipping stuff, however, see the comments below.
Acknowledged

This runs afoul of the following:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/3b986d3a6829eba0c546df7035e095c7abe48ae3/docs/checklists/changes.md#L142-L149

Generally my advice is to avoid decoding the substructures here. Instead, when necessary, we can define iterators (as mentioned in the link). I don't think it's necessary to define them _yet_, as we only want to locate the PDR of interest, which we can do via `pdr->effecter_id` right? It's enough to decode up to `pdr->composite_effecter_count`, as what follows are the substructures that we'd iterate over.

Further, this is an internal API for now, so we can change it around as we see fit.
Acknowledged
This would need to be `return pldm_msgbuf_discard(buf, -ENOMEM);`.
Done

Can't we rather derive found like:

```
found = pdr->effecter_id == effecter_id;
```

? 

We've done all the work to decode the PDR.
Acknowledged
Hi Pavithra, this is looking okay now. I have a couple of minor comments inline.

This can be reduced to

```
return pldm_msgbuf_complete(buf);
```
Done
This condition will never evaluate true as found is either 1 or 0 by the equality test. The code can be removed.
Done
Sorry, I feel like we're going around on this a bit, but we're still making progress. Having dealt with the msgbuf-related concerns, I have some more queries on the control flow.
This is a pointer, is it allowed to be `NULL`? I suggest we allow it, but that must be documented above.
Acknowledged
Should this be `continue` rather than a `return`?
Done
You must ensure `record_handle` is not `NULL` before dereferencing it.
Done
This at least needs `ASSERT_NE(repo, nullptr);`
Done
This hasn't tested any of the error paths? Can you please provide some coverage there?
Done

What do you feel makes this done? What I was asking was that you look at each of the places you return an error in the implementation and provide a corresponding test for that path.

Also, please avoid single test cases that test multiple behaviours. I would like the tests to have a relationship of one behaviour to one test function (a new `TEST(...)` defined for each behaviour exercised), unless they truly are trivial (e.g. where passing `NULL` for a parameter value should result in an error value returned - anything beyond that is non-trivial).

Andrew, in the old patchset, I had added a test case where if the effecter ID is not found, we return, and the number of records in the repo remains the same.

In the new patchset, I have added the test case in the error scenario during the decode of the state effecter. I believe these are the two scenarios where this API could return an error. The trivial case where the parameter is `NULL` is asserted in the test case.

Please suggest to me if you think any other test case should be handled.
Done
